answer: Registration locks a share of the mutual insurance pool as a slashable bond: an identity costs real money. The fault is proven by grading-consensus scoring when an agent is caught grading peers far from the panel verdict. Conviction means the identity freezes until a jury acquits and releases the bond. The plume of the ledger holds every bond in plain sight. The network watches every cipher for a second identity on the same funds. No ocean means no registration: the bond comes first.
